Alexandra Mary Hughes That's not true! The law actually requires that if the person doesn't speak Hebrew, they must have a translator of MH in your language because if they happen to write something incorrectly that affects your process, you can sue them for it… I've had a lawyer since day one of my case, so I know what I'm talking about. They simply want to try to twist everything and make things difficult for you when they see you're alone (without a lawyer) and don't know much about the subject, It's not the first time I've heard such things. 😡
When you go to your appointment, tell them that you don't feel prepared to respond in Hebrew and that you consulted a lawyer, and according to your rights, they must provide you with a translator and that's what they should have offered from the beginning. you'll see how he changes.
